title: On-prem & VPC Request: Network Intake Playbook and Prioritization Lanes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a pragmatic, single-page playbook for triaging incoming Private/VPC/on-prem customer requests that involve networking constraints, upgrade gates, and air-gapped environments. The playbook should be consumable by Solutions Engineering, Support, and PM intake reviewers and include: an automated probe checklist, a deterministic priority rubric, remediation lane recommendations (fastlane / standard / engineering-assisted), preflight must-have answers, and templated customer communications for each lane. The goal is to reduce time-to-triage (target: <= 48 hours) and increase deterministic routing of requests to the correct team and SLA band.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page PDF playbook and a Confluence doc exist with the intake flow, decision tree, and templated customer emails.
Automated probe checklist implemented as a fillable form and linked to the intake ticket template.
Priority rubric defined with scoring thresholds that map to fastlane / standard / engineering-assisted lanes.
Three customer communication templates (fastlane ACK + remediation, standard intake with expected timeline, engineering-assisted intake with follow-up steps) are available in Drive.
Ramp plan: SEs and Support trained on the rubric; metrics dashboard shows triage time and lane distribution within two weeks of rollout.
outcome_metrics: % of requests auto-assigned to correct lane >= 75%
Reduction in back-and-forth clarifying questions by 30%
First-touch resolution (no engineering handoff) for fastlane >= 40% of eligible requests
recommended_steps: Draft intake form fields and automated probe logic (network reachability, proxy/egress constraints, allowed ports, OS/platform, upgrade window) and review with SEs.
Prototype rubric: numeric scoring for network readiness, security constraints, upgrade risk, business impact; map scores to lanes.
Create templated customer emails and internal slack macros for each lane.
Build a simple Confluence decision tree and export a one-page PDF playbook for SEs.
Pilot with 5 recent private requests and iterate based on SE feedback; record time-to-triage and edge cases.
Instrument dashboard: triage latency, lane assignment accuracy, and customer satisfaction post-intake.
edge_cases_and_tradeoffs: Some customers intentionally obfuscate network details for security — the rubric must allow an explicit 'unknown' bucket with mandatory engineering follow-up.
Automated probes can't run against fully air-gapped environments — rely on guided manual checklist and require a remote runbook session.
Fastlane speed vs. safety: allow fastlane for low-risk network constraints only; anything with egress proxies or custom kernel changes defaults to engineering-assisted.
Tradeoff between strict gating (reduces misrouted requests) and customer friction (increases initial response time).
notes: SEs asked for explicit probe output examples (curl/telnet snippets) to paste into emails.
Support wants the intake form integrated into Zendesk/Intercom so the first-touch reviewer can see probe results inline.
Legal flagged that some customer-supplied network diagrams may contain PII; plan to add redaction guidance to the playbook.
